title: Triage Handoff & Stability Patterns — Ops Daily Slate
body:
Purpose:
This working slate captures a lightweight, operational pattern for daily triage handoffs into Product Ops during launch ramps. The goal is to provide a compact KPI gauge, decision lanes, and a reproducible handoff script so engineering and ops teams can act quickly without long meetings.

Context and scope:
- Applies to pre-GA and first 4 weeks of public launches for hosted API and Dedicated offerings.
- Focused on platform-facing signals (latency, error rate, model fallbacks, capacity shortages) and adoption signals that have direct SLO/KPI impact (activation rate, API error budget, cost-per-request).
- Not intended to replace SRE incident runbooks; this is the product ops daily triage and escalation frame.

High-level goals (ranked):
1) Keep user-facing error budget < 2% for the primary path.
2) Maintain p95 latency within target band (see KPI thresholds).
3) Prevent cascading fallbacks by automatic throttles or routing.
4) Identify regressions in quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE proxies, request quality flags) and pause rollouts if needed.

Daily Health Gauge (one-pager to paste into Slack daily-ops channel):
- Date: YYYY-MM-DD
- Primary model/version: <model-name>@<sha>
- Traffic window: 9:00–17:00 PT (current cadence)
- Quick numbers (last 60m):
  - Requests/min: 3,800 — trend: +12%
  - Error rate (4xx+5xx): 1.6% — trend: flat
  - p50/p95 latency (ms): 60 / 420 — p95 above target (target p95=300ms)
  - Fallbacks engaged: 8 (auto-route to smaller model)
  - Cost per 1k tokens (USD): 1.12 — trend: up 8% (due to longer sequences)

KPI mapping and thresholds (operational lane):
- Availability KPI: API success rate >= 98% (warning 97–98, critical <97)
- Latency KPI: p95 <= 300ms (warning 300–450, critical >450)
- Error budget burn: Daily burn rate <= 0.5% (warning single-day >1%, critical multi-day >1%)
- Quality regression: New eval pass rate >= 95% on canary prompt set (warning 90–95, critical <90)
- Cost KPI: cost-per-1k-tokens vs baseline <= +25% (warning +25–40%, critical >40%)

Triage handoff flow (5–10 minute structured exchange):
1) Reporter posts health gauge to #product-ops-daily and tags on-call SRE + PM on duty. Include timestamped screenshot of dashboard and the 60m quick numbers.
2) On-call SRE validates whether symptoms match an Incident (latency spikes, >5% 5xx, capacity OOMs). If yes, escalate via incident runbook (SRE). If no, proceed as Product Ops triage.
3) Product Ops PM opens/updates tracker row with: impact statement, affected customers, probable cause, priority (P0/P1/P2), linked JIRA key, owner for next 2 hours.
4) Quick actions (choose any that applies): scale capacity, enable short-term traffic-shape, rollback model variant, toggle caching TTLs, or initiate targeted canary revert.
5) Re-evaluate in 30 minutes; if metrics improve to warning->normal, close the triage entry and run a short post-mortem note; if not, escalate to incident.

Stability patterns (common root causes + typical mitigations):
- Pattern: Gradual p95 drift with flat error rate.
  - Cause: Longer sequence lengths (client-side change) or tail token distribution shift.
  - Mitigation: Apply adaptive batching throttle, reduce max_tokens for the gateway, or deploy quantized variant with same quality profile.
- Pattern: Sudden spike in 5xx from a single region.
  - Cause: Hardware node eviction or kernel failure.
  - Mitigation: Auto-evacuate pool, failover to secondary region, notify infra on-call, temporary rate-limiter for that region.
- Pattern: Quality regressions with low latency.
  - Cause: New model variant rollout or tokenizer mismatch.
  - Mitigation: Pause rollout, pin traffic to previous model, run targeted evaluation harness against failing prompts.

Decision lanes (clear actions tied to threshold crossings):
- Green -> Observe: KPI in target band. No action required beyond daily note.
- Amber -> Contain + Watch: KPI in warning band. Product Ops action: assign owner, short mitigation (scale/route), re-check 30m.
- Red -> Escalate: KPI in critical band. Trigger incident path; SRE leads; Product Ops coordinates customer comms and rollback choices.

Ownership matrix (quick reference):
- Product Ops PM (on-duty): coordinates cross-team, updates tracker, customer comms.
- Serving-runtime Eng: investigate kernel/quantization regressions and capacity decisions.
- Infra/SRE: node health, region failover, autoscaler adjustments.
- Developer Experience / SDK: if issues trace to client-side changes, produce quick patch.

Handoff checklist (script to paste into ticket or Slack):
- Summary: one-sentence impact description
- Time window and link to dashboard snapshot
- Primary KPI values (success rate, p95, cost delta)
- Recent changes (deploys, config changes, model rollouts) with PR/Jira links
- Suggested immediate action (scale/rollback/throttle)
- Owner for next 2 hours
- Customer exposure list (top 3 affected orgs)

Runbook snippets (cut-and-paste):
Slack alert template:
"[DAILY TRIAGE] {date} {env} {model}@{ver} — p95={p95}ms err={err_rate}% requests/min={rps}. Suggested: {suggested_action}. Owner: @{owner}. Dash: {dash_link}"

Quick CLI to pin traffic to safe model variant (example):
# pin traffic to variant stable-v1 for service 'api-hosted'
redwoodctl rollout set --service api-hosted --variant stable-v1 --duration 30m --reason "daily-triage-stable-pin"

Customer comms template (short):
Subject: Temporary mitigation for degraded API latency
Body: Hi {customer}, we observed increased latency on {date/time} affecting some requests. We applied a temporary routing mitigation and the team is actively investigating root cause. We do not expect request loss to continue; will follow up with a post-incident summary.

Post-triage notes (what to capture after resolution):
- Root cause summary (one paragraph)
- Timeline of actions with timestamps
- Metrics before/after
- Follow-ups (engineering work items and owners)
- Retrospective action if pattern repeats

Open questions / trade-offs to decide this week:
- When do we prefer model rollback vs. traffic pin? (tradeoff: short-term user experience vs. potential quality regression)
- Rebalance cost vs. latency for high-sequence workloads — should product ops own a temporary cost waiver flow?
- Hand-off cadence: is a single daily readout sufficient for launches with >20k RPS?

Next steps / work items (short backlog):
- Create dashboard widget for "canary prompt quality delta" (owner: Sofia) — JIRA PRODOPS-4890
- Add CLI shortcut in redwoodctl for "daily-triage-pin" (owner: Liam) — PR #1273
- Run a dry-run handoff exercise with SRE and serving-runtime next Wednesday 10:00 PT (owner: Maya)

Notes to self:
- Keep this slate intentionally concise: product ops needs rapid decisioning not verbose narrative.
- Archive final decisions to Confluence page linked above for audits.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-03 — initial draft (Maya)
- 2025-11-12 — added decision lanes and runbook snippets (Liam)
- 2025-11-19 — in_review edits and KPI threshold tuning after ramp test (Sofia)
